statement: The required ci.yml gate job must be able to finish the proof a product change obliges: attempt 1 lifts the job's timeout-minutes from 120 to the GitHub maximum of 360 for every event (PR #184's gate run 41431327759 was killed by the 120-minute limit with its exclusive lane at 73 of 103 files); attempt 2 routes same-repository pull-request gates to the lab's self-hosted Linux runners, designed first and changed only after the lead's decision.

constraints.statement: Only .github/workflows/ci.yml, test/manifests/ci-resource-plan.json, the hardening contract that asserts ci.yml, CHANGELOG.md and this quest's records; never formation-health.yml, never a dispatched workflow, never a runner registration by the implementer.
No dual routing path: the gate has one runs-on expression owned by the resource plan; an absent lab runner is a visible queued job with a named operator answer, not a silent fallback.
Attempt 2 changes no workflow until the lead decides the design note.

supersession.statement: pull-request gates stay on the hosted runner by owner policy (home-lab.md) and the lead's acceptance of the attempt-2 recommendation; the lab-routing design is retained as evidence for a future owner decision (docs/evidence/ci-gate-proof-time-2026-11/lab-runner-routing-design-note.md). The sealed doneWhen is immutable (solve land refuses a changed probe), so the claim that can be proved without a routing implementation is carried by the successor quest ci-gate-proof-time-maximum.
